# Duṭṭhaṭṭhaka Sutta (Snp 4.3 (PTS Snp 153))

**ID:** Snp 4.3 (PTS Snp 153)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Duṭṭhaṭṭhaka Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duṭṭhaṭṭhaka Sutta* ("Eight on Malice" or "Corruption") is the third discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* (verses 780–787) [Anderson and Smith 1913; Hazra 1994; Saddhatissa 2013]. It is one of only four poems in the collection that strictly fulfill the literal definition of an *aṭṭhaka* ("octave") by consisting of exactly eight stanzas [Hazra 1994]. Along with other discourses of the *Aṭṭhakavagga*, the sutta deals with debate (*vāda*), malice (*duṭṭhamanas*), and grasping at views (*diṭṭhupādāna*) [Jayatilleke 1963; Anālayo 2010; Saddhatissa 2013].

The text opens by observing that people speak in debate either out of malice or out of the conviction that they alone hold the truth; the sage (*muni*), however, does not enter into any dispute and remains free from obstruction [Saddhatissa 2013; Anderson and Smith 1913]. Freedom and liberation cannot be found through dogmatic attachment, boasting of one's precepts, or seeking victory in intellectual controversy [Jayatilleke 1963; Anālayo 2010; Kuan 2008]. Instead, the wise person (*dhona*), having relinquished preconceptions, neither grasps nor rejects anything in this world and has shaken off all speculative views [Müller 1881; Pande 1974; Lamotte 1980].

A resembling parallel is preserved in the Chinese translation of the *Arthavargīya* (*Foshuo yizu jing*, T 198). In addition, citations corresponding to verse 787 are found in the Sanskrit *Arthavargīya* traditions preserved in the *Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra* [Lamotte 1980]. Within the Pali Canon, the sutta is commented upon word for word in the canonical *Duṭṭhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 3) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus registers 67 Pali-internal text-reuse matches, most extensively with Mnd 3 (45 matches), as well as with the commentaries *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
